host.description: The hostname used to access Grafana externally (defaults to 'grafana' subdomain for the tenant host).

storageClassName.description: StorageClass used to store the data.

tracingStorages.description: Configuration of traces storage instances. Empty by default (tracing off): no backend and no trace collector are rendered. Adding an entry provisions a VictoriaTraces backend and, while tracingCollector.enabled is true, deploys the OTLP collector in front of it. A tenant with shared-central tracing (the Tenant's tracingCentral) gets the collector, while tracingCollector.enabled is true, without an entry, which then exports to the shared store; entries still listed keep their store and datasource, so traces stored before the switch stay readable until the entry is removed.

mode.description: Deployment mode: "cluster" renders a VTCluster; "single" renders a single-binary VTSingle for edge/dev/small clusters. Treat as immutable once a backend exists: mode selects which Kind is rendered under the same name, so changing it on a running backend re-identifies the object rather than reconfiguring it. Switching from "single" to "cluster" prunes the VTSingle and the operator garbage-collects its PVC (stored traces are lost); switching from "cluster" to "single" (or removing the entry) leaves the vtstorage PVCs Bound and billed until the whole Monitoring release is deleted. The API cannot guard this (transition rules are not available on an array-item field), so this note is the only guard: migrate deliberately, accepting the loss.

name.description: Name of the storage instance: a lowercase RFC 1123 label of at most 42 characters. Treat as immutable once a backend exists: the VTCluster/VTSingle, its Services, PVCs and Grafana datasource are all named after it, so renaming an entry deploys a new, empty backend and removes the old one, the same way changing mode does (single mode loses the old PVC, cluster mode leaves the old vtstorage PVCs Bound until the whole Monitoring release is deleted).

retentionDiskUsageBytes.description: Optional disk-usage cap as a VictoriaMetrics BytesString (e.g. "8GB" or "8GiB"), bounding disk use on top of the age-based retentionPeriod. Uses byte-suffix grammar (kb/mb/gb/tb, KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB), NOT the Kubernetes-quantity grammar of the sibling storage field, so "8Gi" is rejected by the operator. In cluster mode the cap is per vtstorage replica (replicaCount 2), so the effective total is twice the value. Unset, the store drops its oldest day once its filesystem is 80% full instead, so every store is disk-bounded. Either way VictoriaTraces keeps the last two days, so spans arriving faster than the cap allows for two days can still fill the disk.

storageClassName.description: StorageClass used to store the data.

tracingCentralHost.description: tenant-root only: accept spans from tenants that turned on shared-central tracing (the Tenant's tracingCentral) into this Monitoring's tracingStorages entry named `generic`, which must be in `cluster` mode. Every central tenant then shares that store's disk and retention with tenant-root, and nothing reserves space per tenant: once the store's disk cap is reached (retentionDiskUsageBytes, or 80% of its filesystem) the oldest spans of all of them are evicted together. Each tenant is held to the platform's monitoring.tracingCentralTenantBytesPerSecond, which by default lets one tenant write at most the cap of a default 10Gi store, counted uncompressed, over the two days VictoriaTraces always keeps, so raise it with the store; several tenants writing at their limit together still can fill it. Ignored outside tenant-root. The tenant-root namespace is inside the trust boundary of the shared store, as it is for the metrics of tenants that rely on a parent's monitoring: vmauth pins each central tenant to its own account, but workloads in tenant-root reach the store directly, and one that learns a tenant's account ID (a hash of its namespace name and UID, which its VMUser carries) can read and write that account. Whoever tenant-root admits to its Grafana is inside it too, since tenant-root's own datasource for the store reaches vtselect without vmauth; who that is follows its Grafana's oidc mode (with System, tenant-root's own groups, which already hold the same access level in every tenant under tenant-root). The render refuses to stop hosting while central tenants remain, but removing the tenant-root Monitoring altogether is not a render and is not refused: turn tracingCentral off on the central tenants first, since until then every Monitoring render of theirs fails, their metrics, logs and alerting changes included. The refusals read each other's objects when they render, so a tenant turning tracingCentral on while tenant-root stops hosting can pass both: that tenant's collector then exports to a vmauth that is gone while every release reports Ready, until its Monitoring renders again. Recover by hosting again; turning that tenant's tracingCentral off instead ends the silent drop, and turning it on again is then refused until tenant-root hosts.

tracingCollector.description: OpenTelemetry Collector for trace ingestion. With shared-central tracing it refuses spans above the platform's per-tenant write rate: OTLP/HTTP senders retry them, OTLP/gRPC senders drop them, so export over HTTP.

enabled.description: Deploy the OTLP collector. When disabled, applications must send OTLP straight to the traces backend (no central sampling/redaction); with shared-central tracing they have no path to it, so no new spans arrive, while the traces already stored stay readable. The collector fronts a single backend, and the limit holds with shared-central tracing too, since turning that off makes it export to the local entry again: while it is enabled, tracingStorages must hold at most one entry, and adding a second one fails the whole Monitoring render until the extra entry is removed or the collector is disabled.

redactAttributes.description: Span attribute keys to drop before export (the PII/secret control point, e.g. db.statement).

replicas.description: Number of collector replicas. Head sampling is trace-id-deterministic, so replicas>1 are safe and remove the single-ingest-path SPOF. With shared-central tracing each replica sends up to two requests at a time against this tenant's limit of four per vmauth replica, which its Grafana reads share, so more replicas do not raise the tenant's throughput and can slow its reads; the tenant's write rate (the platform's monitoring.tracingCentralTenantBytesPerSecond) is split across them as well, so a sender whose connection stays on one replica gets that replica's share, and each replica that starts lets up to 4 MiB through above the rate.

samplingPercentage.description: Head-sampling percentage applied at the collector before export.

email.description: Configuration for email alerts. Alerts carrying the label notify_email with the string value true are emailed when their severity is in the severities list (default critical and major). A bare YAML boolean does not match. Alerts listed in alertnames are emailed unless matched by an earlier platform route.

alertnames.description: Alert names emailed whether or not the rule carries the notify_email label, with no severity filter. Earlier platform routes still take precedence. Alerts with `event="Heartbeat"`, including `Watchdog`, go only to Alerta, and alerts with severity `none`, `CDIDefaultStorageClassDegraded` and `CDINoDefaultStorageClass` are blackholed and never reach email. This is the way to opt in alerts the platform ships, since their helm-owned rule definitions cannot be labelled per cluster. Entries must be plain Prometheus alert names such as `KubeAPIDown`, and anything else fails the render. Empty adds no extra route.

authUsername.description: Username for SMTP LOGIN/PLAIN authentication. The password is read from the `password` key of a Secret named `alertmanager-email-password` in the release namespace, which the platform operator creates. The name is fixed and the Secret is mounted into Alertmanager, so a missing Secret blocks the whole Alertmanager rollout, not only email delivery. The credential in it must belong to this tenant alone. `smarthost` is chosen by whoever writes the Monitoring, so one relay credential provisioned under the same name in every namespace can be collected by pointing `smarthost` at a host the tenant controls.

from.description: Sender address, one only. A display name is accepted. It takes the same narrower form as `to`, and an address outside it fails the render.

repeatInterval.description: Minimum time before a still-firing alert is emailed again, as an Alertmanager duration with units `y`, `w`, `d`, `h`, `m`, `s`, `ms` in descending order, each at most once, such as `5m`, `12h` or `1h30m`. Delivery is evaluated every 5m, so shorter intervals take effect at 5m and other intervals round up to a multiple of 5m. Zero, a unit out of order and a total beyond what Alertmanager accepts fail the render. Empty keeps the 12h default.

severities.description: Severities the notify_email route accepts (e.g. ["critical","major","warning"]). Empty keeps the default of critical and major. List every severity in use to email opted-in alerts regardless of severity. Entries must be plain severity names, and anything else fails the render.

smarthost.description: SMTP server as `host:port` (e.g. "smtp.example.com:465"). A value without a port, an invalid bracketed IP address or a port with leading zeros fails the render. Port 465 uses implicit TLS, other ports use STARTTLS.

to.description: Recipient address, or several separated by commas. A display name is accepted, such as `Oncall <oncall@example.org>`, as long as it carries no comma. Quote display names containing punctuation such as `:`, `@`, parentheses or `?`. RFC 2047 encoded words are not accepted. IP domain literals accept dotted-quad IPv4 only. IPv6 literals are rejected because Go mail parsers disagree on their syntax across versions. ASCII control characters are rejected. Addresses must be literal, so Alertmanager template actions are rejected. The accepted form is deliberately narrower than RFC 5322. The local part must be a dot-atom, with no leading, trailing or doubled dot, and quoted local parts, comments and a `mailto:` prefix are rejected. An address outside that form fails the render, because Alertmanager parses addresses only when it sends and drops the notification with no record a tenant can read.

chatID.description: Telegram chat ID(s), separated by commas.

storage.description: Persistent volume size for the database.

size.description: Persistent volume size for the database.

externalLabels.description: External labels applied to all metrics.

oidc.description: OIDC authentication for the Grafana instance. See docs/oidc-grafana.md for the operator guide.

customConfig.description: Tenant-supplied `[auth.generic_oauth]` payload; consumed only when `mode: CustomConfig`.

config.description: Inline map of `[auth.generic_oauth]` keys. Written verbatim into the Grafana CR `spec.config`. Mutually exclusive with `secretRef.name`.

secretRef.description: Reference to a Secret holding an `auth.ini` fragment; mounted under `/etc/grafana/oidc` and loaded via `GF_PATHS_CUSTOM_INI`.

name.description: Name of an existing Secret in the release namespace whose `auth.ini` key holds a ready-made `[auth.generic_oauth]` block. Mutually exclusive with `customConfig.config`.

mode.description: Identity mode. `None`: no OIDC, only the `grafana-admin-password` Secret works. `System`: trust the platform `cozy` realm via a per-instance confidential client and audience binding; zero-config default. `CustomConfig`: trust a tenant-supplied issuer directly (BYO); `cozy` is not in the path.

users.description: Users granted access to this Grafana instance's org. Each entry is reconciled into Grafana org membership + role by a chart-owned post-install/post-upgrade Job. Works for both `System` and `CustomConfig` modes; ignored when `mode: None`. Users not listed here get nothing (no default org role from group mapping).

email.description: Email address matched against the `email` claim from the issuer. The chart pre-provisions a Grafana account with this email so the users-Job can set the org role before the operator's first login (`oauth_allow_insecure_email_lookup = true` glues the two together). Must match a conservative pattern: local part is `[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+`, domain is `[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}`. Whitespace, quoted literals, and unusual URL-reserved characters are rejected on schema level so the reconcile-Job's shell handling never has to defend against malformed input.

role.description: Grafana org role to bind: `Admin`, `Editor`, or `Viewer`. Applied to the release's Grafana org (`Main Org.`); server-level `GrafanaAdmin` promotion is out of scope for Phase 1. Required — the users-Job POSTs `{loginOrEmail, role}` to `/api/orgs/1/users` and PATCHes `{role}` to converge across re-runs; omitting the field would render `role: "null"` into the body and fail with HTTP 400.
